provenance: Official source: yes. These figures are BetaNYC's, derived from it, not an official NYC Office of Technology and Innovation (OTI) report.

BoardStat (BetaNYC) pulls OTI's dataset from NYC Open Data, the City's open data portal, every night and publishes files at https://www.beta.nyc/boardstat/data/. This server downloads those files once per BoardStat build and reads them on this machine.

Changed by BetaNYC: Requests created before 2020-01-01 are left out. Each request with usable coordinates is placed in a community district and a Council district by BetaNYC's own point-in-polygon join against the City's current district boundaries, not the City's own district fields. Problem names are grouped where the City spells one two ways. Requests are counted by district, month, problem type, agency and address. ZIP codes are dropped.

The numbers match the BoardStat page each answer links to. Caveat: 311 counts are reports, not problems: they show who reports and how, not only how many problems there are. 'Closed' does not mean fixed. Caveat: BoardStat's files are under the Open Database License (ODbL) 1.0; the City's records in them stay under NYC Open Data's terms.
